opportunity: kuna recovers composite layouts and then shows them only on the whole-program surface. `kuna decompile ./fmt get_prefix` prints `int get_prefix(_IO_FILE *f)` and field accesses against a layout nothing in the output describes; reaching that layout means exporting a whole `decompile-project` folder for one function. angr prints the typedefs a function references above it, which is a large part of why its output reads struct-aware. kuna had the renderer (`PrintC::doc_type_definitions`, the `docTypeDefinitions` port) and only a whole-project caller for it.
test_name: tests/stages/kuna-structdefs.xml (5 assertions, two `print C` passes over one decompiled function) + 7 unit tests in kuna_structdefs/tests.rs + tests/cli/structdefs-json-types-array.json and -key-off.json
inspiration: angr's decompiler prints the typedefs a function references above it (analyses/decompiler/structured_codegen/c.py)

in_repo_repro_walk_list.after: typedef struct Node Node; | struct Node { int val; undefined1 _pad4[4]; Node *next; }; | int walk_list(Node *n)
in_repo_repro_walk_list.why: the self-referential case: the forward declaration is what lets the body reference `Node *next` inside `struct Node`, which is the kuna divergence from upstream's anonymous `typedef struct {...} name;` form

unstripped_fmt_get_prefix.after: typedef struct _IO_marker _IO_marker; /* opaque */ | typedef struct _IO_FILE _IO_FILE; | struct _IO_FILE { int _flags; undefined1 _pad4[4]; char *_IO_read_ptr; ... }; | int get_prefix(_IO_FILE *f)

stripped_fmt_libctypes.after: typedef struct FILE FILE; /* opaque */ | void sub_2f30(FILE *a0) // return-dupe

json_types_array.note: one record per name: the factory's forward-declared _IO_FILE is dropped in favour of the complete one (dedup_by_name)

witnesses.structsynth_pair: not run: #655 (structsynth) is an unmerged draft in another worktree; this option is independent of it and renders a synthesized struct_N by the same path a DWARF or libctypes type takes

sweep.method: whole-binary `decompile-all` over six binaries, this build vs a main build (fc7c7a22, which differs from 83830e86 only by the default-off ptrfromuse), then this build with the option on vs off, every unified-diff hunk classified by classify-hunks.py

on_vs_off_hunks.classification: every hunk is a pure insertion of type-definition text above a function; no body line moved, changed or disappeared
on_vs_off_hunks.distribution: 8071 of 8657 added lines are on ls, the one unstripped binary (DWARF gives most functions a real multi-field struct); the five stripped binaries average 117 added lines each

benchmark.reason: decbench type_match reads the --json variables[] array, which this option does not touch; the C text it does touch is read only for functions whose variables[] is empty. No typesweep was run: there is no channel by which a preamble above a function can move a variable's type.
benchmark.new_surface: functions[].types[] is additive and no metric reads it yet; it exists so scripts/decbench/structscore.py's layout side can read a recovered layout from the per-function record instead of parsing the project header.

speed.default_cost: one bool test (`if !self.options.struct_defs { return; }`) per function document

on_arm.method: interleaved off/on, min-of-21, `kuna decompile-all --addr 0x2f30` on unstripped fmt (the DWARF _IO_FILE case, the largest preamble one function gets in the corpus)
on_arm.verdict: within the noise of this box for a single function (the two runs disagree in sign); the process is dominated by spawn + load. A first median-based timeit run reported +5.5%/+6.5% while the corpus sweep was running, which is why the minimum is the statistic reported.
on_arm.caveat: three test lanes and several sibling agents ran throughout; on one run the OFF median came out ABOVE the ON median (235ms vs 177ms).

whole_binary.method: interleaved off/on with the leading arm alternating per iteration, min-of-11, whole-binary `kuna decompile-all` on stripped fmt (151 functions, 36 of which name a composite)

earlier_run.note: same measurement before the alternating order, under heavier load

whole_binary.verdict: a real ON-arm cost of roughly +6-8% on a whole-binary run: the walk is per function over that function's Varnodes and runs twice when the JSON surface is also asked for. The default path is untouched (one bool test), which is why this is an opt-in flag and not a preset entry.

speed.default_off_reason: presentation default, not a speed hold: a preamble above every function is noise for a caller diffing bodies or feeding one function to a matcher.

consistency.decompile_project_unchanged: byte-identical export with the option on, serially, under --jobs 2 and under --stream (the bodies include the .h that already carries the definitions; decompile_pulled clears the flag for a want_proto batch)
consistency.renderer: printc::render_type_definitions, the same function that builds the .h type block
consistency.line_numbers: the preamble is emitted through the emitter before begin_function, not prepended to the finished string, so line_mappings and variables[].line_numbers count it the same way `code` does (walk_list with the option on: line_mappings[0].line_number == 13 == the `if (n) {` line)
consistency.output_language: the preamble and the JSON types array decline for a non-C output language: the renderer builds the project .h, so its output is C, and a `struct X { ... };` block in a Rust document is neither valid Rust nor readable C. decompile-project refuses a non-C language outright for the same reason. Probe: tests/cli/structdefs-declines-a-rust-document.json

notes: The roots of the type walk (prototype, every Varnode type, every mapped Symbol type) are deliberately a superset of the names the printer spells, so the preamble cannot omit a definition the body refers to; the cost is that a type carried by a Varnode that contributes no token can be defined above a function that never names it.
preset_decision: EXCLUDED_ON_PURPOSE in p0_knowledge/modes.rs: not in AGGRESSIVE_OVERRIDES. The preset is the default output under 500 KiB -- the text a caller diffs, feeds to a matcher, or reads one function of -- and a preamble in front of every function that touches a FILE * is noise there (36 of fmt's 151 functions would repeat the same `typedef struct FILE FILE;`; ls alone is 8,071 added lines). Nothing about the option is wrong output; who wants to see a layout is a reader's choice, not a size threshold's.
